2.name: good
2.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
identifiable peak corrupted by low firing

5.name: 0rhythm
5.notes:
pyr-pyr (hotkey 8)
---
broad peak (>1ms wide) symmetric to time 0

6.name: rhythm
6.notes:
pyr-pyr (hotkey 9)
---
set of multiple, evenly spaced peaks likely entrained to an oscillation

7.name: burst
7.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
target neuron is later spikes in source neuron burst, not an individual unit. Characterized by very broad double peaks on the positive time axis around 5-10 ms and very low co-firing on the negative time axis.

8.name: ok
8.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
suspicious peak that has a chance of being real, hindered by extremely low SNR

10.name: 2peakms
10.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
two sharp peaks (<.5ms wide) forming a rift symmetric to 0ms

11.name: pos_skew
11.notes:
pyr-pyr, pyr-int
---
preferentially high co-activity on the positive end of the time axis

12.name: leak
12.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
Speculated leak between parts of the same neuron classified as two different units.
Or, an ultra-sharp peak at 0ms that might be spurious.

16.name: I-I-flip
16.notes:
int-int
---
inhibition <0ms (is an I-I inhibitory pair if you flip ref and target)

18.name: Disinhib
18.notes:
pyr-int
---
Significant dip <0ms followed by significant peak at synaptic timescale
Disinhibition pairs can be valid pyr-ints; they should be selectively included when counting best/good pairs

20.name: rift
20.notes:
pyr-int
---
Similar to 2peakms, but instead of having two visible peaks flanking there is just a sharp dip at 0ms

25.name: neg_skew
25.notes:
INT-PYR
---
baseline decreases after inhibitiory dip

29.name: bad
29.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
not bad enough to be deleted but unlikely to identify any valid patterns

32.name: triple
32.notes:
pyr-pyr
---
group of 3 or more sharp peak centered around zero with strong cleaves

33.name: lateWidePeak
33.notes:
pyr-int
---
3-5ms very wide peak likely due to oscillatory coupling
